comparison: Both evaluate program description and scope (C1-C3, C19-C24). OpenEval finds detailed, consistent documentation of program design. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'the internship program is well described' and note good sample size and response rates. Strong agreement on program description quality.

Both assess intern survey outcomes (C26-C38). OpenEval finds data supported with appropriate statistics and adequate response rates. Peer reviewers accept findings without challenge, with editor noting data 'convincingly show the benefit of internships to students and postdocs.' Strong agreement on intern benefits.

Both address qualitative focus group findings (C39-C63). OpenEval emphasizes mixed-methods strength and longitudinal design. Peer reviewers accept findings as part of overall positive outcomes, noting benefits to research advisors and improved communication. Agreement on qualitative data value.

Both evaluate host/employer outcomes (C64-C72). OpenEval finds nuanced, credible pre-post data with appropriate statistics. Peer reviewers accept findings, with editor noting data show benefits 'to potential employers' and reviewer noting 'positive outcomes for hosts.' Strong agreement.

Both assess career matching logistic regression (C73-C90). OpenEval finds well-designed analysis with appropriate controls and substantial effect size. Peer reviewers acknowledge findings but note 'the study design cannot determine whether this is a causal relationship.' Agreement on findings with shared caution about causality.

Both evaluate career outcome differences (C91-C106). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to self-selection bias acknowledged by authors. Peer reviewers accept descriptive findings (lower postdoc rates, more science-related careers) while also noting observational design limits causal inference. Strong agreement on limitation.

Both assess productivity/publication outcomes (C107-C111). OpenEval finds appropriate statistical comparisons showing no evidence of harm. Peer reviewers strongly affirm, with editor noting benefits 'without adverse impacts on scientific productivity' and reviewer stating data 'refute one of the principle concerns of research advisors.' Strong agreement.

Both evaluate faculty attitude changes (C112-C117). OpenEval finds clear pre-post comparison with appropriate statistics. Peer reviewers accept finding, with reviewer noting paper 'will be very useful...to dispel some of the concerns of research advisers.' Strong agreement on faculty shift.

Both address internship timing and structure preferences (C121, C125-C138). OpenEval finds consistency across data sources on optimal duration. Peer reviewers implicitly accept through acknowledgment of 'lessons learned for other institutions' and program design features. Agreement on structural findings.

Both evaluate factors affecting internship success (C131-C138). OpenEval finds logical, well-articulated qualitative themes. Peer reviewers implicitly accept as part of 'lessons learned' that will help other institutions. Agreement on practical guidance.

Both assess program operational components (C139-C149). OpenEval finds concrete, well-documented program features. Peer reviewers accept as part of well-described program with 'clearly defined' outcomes. Strong agreement on program structure.

Both evaluate satisfaction data across stakeholders (C150-C165). OpenEval finds extensive, consistent high satisfaction with specific percentages. Peer reviewers accept as part of convincing benefit demonstration. Agreement on satisfaction outcomes, though peer review emphasizes host satisfaction specifically.

Both address international trainee challenges (C181-C190). OpenEval finds honest acknowledgment of visa and funding barriers. Peer reviewers implicitly accept through acknowledgment of overall methodology and limitations. Agreement on operational challenges.

Both evaluate funding model and sustainability (C191-C200). OpenEval finds clear documentation of transition and strategic reasoning. Peer reviewers explicitly engage with funding discussion, noting 'wider adoption...will depend...on availability of resources' and suggesting NIH funding mechanisms. Strong agreement with active engagement.

Both assess major program achievements (C5, C6, C204, C225-C226). OpenEval finds outcomes supported by statistical evidence. Peer reviewers accept faculty attitude shift and overall benefits. Agreement on key achievements.

Both evaluate summary of major findings (C201-C213). OpenEval finds accurate summary supported by earlier data. Peer reviewers accept overall findings as convincing demonstration of benefits. Strong agreement on main conclusions.

Both address resource requirements (C232-C236). OpenEval finds transparent, useful information for replication. Peer reviewers implicitly accept through acknowledgment that 'wider adoption...will depend...on availability of resources.' Agreement on resource needs.

Both evaluate postdoc internship challenges (C237-C245). OpenEval finds honest documentation of difficulties while acknowledging value. Peer reviewers explicitly note findings may not apply 'to postdoctoral fellows' and paper useful for 'PhD students (although not necessarily for postdoctoral fellows).' Strong agreement on postdoc limitations.

Both assess generalizability limitations and alternatives (C259-C267). OpenEval finds honest acknowledgment with reasonable adaptations. Peer reviewers accept through statement that paper provides 'lessons learned for other institutions' and discussion of implementation challenges. Agreement on geographic limitations.

Both address self-selection bias and causal inference limitations (C268-C269, C99-C101). OpenEval finds appropriate scientific caution. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge 'the authors acknowledge that limitation that the study subjects were self-selected' and note favorable outcomes may not generalize. Strong agreement on key limitation.

Both evaluate suggestions for future research (C270-C273). OpenEval finds methodologically sound RCT suggestion with ethical considerations. Peer reviewers' statement that work 'should stimulate further research' aligns with authors' future directions. Agreement on research needs.

Both address program enhancement recommendations (C274-C277). OpenEval finds reasonable suggestions for structured reflection and multi-institutional research. Peer reviewers' call for further research on broad implementation aligns with authors' recommendations. Agreement on future directions.
